main_body: A bare, snow-dusted birch-like tree: a tall pale trunk with a branching dark canopy of bare twigs and small snow patches on top, with a small snow mound at the base.
top_band: none - the column scan runs from bare branches down the trunk (white/grey bark with dark marks), with no horizontal top surface; it is a vertical organic trunk.
evidence: The object is an organic tree: trunk and branching twigs drawn as a vertical silhouette. It has no box-like horizontal top or front face, so the 3/4 top-and-front contract does not apply in the usual way. The column scan at x=16 shows only trunk bark (L=206 with dark marks) and a snow patch at the base. The branches spread, and the snow clumps give a few light spots, but there is no readable top surface. Being strict, the trunk reads as a flat elevation with no foreshortened top and no canopy volume, so it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 9 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours for the references. Its dark edge pixels are 100% neutral, so the outline is a near-black grey line, not a tinted material tone. The trunk is a thin grey/white column with 3 tonal steps (white, light grey, dark) and sparse snow highlights. It has no leaf-clump volume and no per-material ramp, so it looks far thinner and more sticker-like than the full, richly shaded Beodeul canopies.
